html:
The Interstate Highway System is the network of motorways that crosses the United States, begun in 1956 and today around 48,000 miles (77,000 km) long.

President Dwight D. Eisenhower pushed for it. As a young officer in 1919 he had crossed the country in an army convoy that took two months on bad roads, and in the Second World War he saw Germany's autobahns. The Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956 had the federal government pay about 90 percent of the cost, from a tax on fuel. Defence was one of the reasons given.

It changed American life:

  • Trucks took over much freight from the railways.
  • Families moved to the suburbs and drove to work.
  • Motels, fast food chains and shopping malls grew along the exits.
  • In many cities the new roads were driven straight through poor, often Black, neighbourhoods, destroying homes and splitting communities. Protests, called freeway revolts, stopped some routes.

The original plan was declared complete in 1992. It remains the backbone of how goods and people move across the country.
sum: The Interstate Highway System is the network of motorways that crosses the United States, begun in 1956 and today around 48,000 miles (77,000 km) long.
